newsitem.title: ZAIRE: Troops disperse Zaire march to back rebel talks.
newsitem.headline: Troops disperse Zaire march to back rebel talks.

text.p: Soldiers broke up a bid by Zaire's main opposition to march in the capital Kinshasa on Friday in support of talks with rebel leader Laurent Kabila but party militants vowed to regroup and try again on Saturday.

Soldiers from the feared Civil Guard patrolled flashpoints in the city after dispersing opposition militants trying to gather at the central train station in the city centre to march in defiance of a government ban of all demonstrations.

Jean Claude Mabale, an activist of the radical Union for Democracy and Social Progress (UDPS) party, whistled a small crowd to attention, shouting support for Kabila even though some 30 gendarmes stood nearby.
"Hello Kabila. You have taken Tingi Tingi. You are taking Kisangani. We are waiting for you in Kinshasa," Mabale, bedecked with party flag and T-shirt, shouted.
Witnesses said UDPS secretary-general Adrien Phongo was beaten and arrested by soldiers from the civil guard.
"They arrested the secretary general Mr Phongo. They hit him with a truncheon and took him away," said Lofudu Cosmos, a local UDPS leader from the swarming working class suburb of Matete.
Three other leading UDPS members -- Professor Mathieu Kalele, Olivier Kabango, and Modesse Sadiki -- were also arrested, witnesses said.
There was no official confirmation of the arrests.
Laurent Mbayo, a senior adviser of UDPS leader Etienne Tshisekedi, said the march was organised to demand tripartite negotiations between Tshisekedi, Kabila and ailing President Mobutu Sese Seko.

UDPS militants in the working class Matonge district said they would march to demand the resignation of Prime Minister Kengo wa Dondo and Mobutu, who is currently at his villa in the south of France. They vowed to try again on Saturday.
Kengo's spokesman, Pascale Dema, said troops had been deployed to prevent the march, called in defiance of last month's government ban on all demonstrations.
"It was a provocation. The government has banned all demonstrations during the state of emergency and until the end of the war with Kabila," he said.
Armed units of the Civil Guard deployed at corners all along the route of the planned march. Only a few dozen would-be marchers succeeded in reaching the departure point.

Mobutu underwent cancer surgery in Europe in August followed by radiation treatment but returned home in December to reshuffle the army and government to respond to the rebel threat in the east. He has since returned twice to Europe.
Aides say there is no cause for concern over his health but the timing of his return to Zaire is unclear.

The Tutsi-led rebels took up arms in October accusing the Zairean authorities of denying them citizenship and planning to expel them to Rwanda, their ancestral home. They hold towns and territory in the east.
They responded to a much-heralded January 20 government counter-offensive by attacking on several fronts, advancing into the mineral-producing southern province of Shaba and pushing north and west.

They have pushed as far west as Kindu and say they are poised to attack Zaire's third city of Kisangani, strategically placed on the Zaire River and headquarters of the army's operations in the war zone.
Zaire accuses Uganda, Rwanda and Burundi of invading in support of the rebels. All deny the charge.
The rebels demand talks with Mobutu on his departure. Zaire rejects that out of hand. The rebels say a March 19 regional summit in Kenya, which excludes them, will achieve nothing.
